task: Implement the first post-stack-lock ED-Finder V3 Svelte foundation on the existing target branch frontend/svelte-foundation. Read README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/development/v3-application-stack-decision.md, CLAUDE.md and current CI/Cypress workflows first. This is a real implementation slice, but it MUST NOT deploy anything, touch production/server/database state, apply migrations, implement Babylon runtime, remove the React/R3F reference app, or begin feature-porting Finder/Planner/etc. Create the new V3 web application at apps/web; keep frontend/ intact as migration/reference evidence and keep its current protected tests running. Use the locked stack: Svelte 5 + SvelteKit 2 static SPA via adapter-static, TypeScript 6 initial compiler, Vite 8/Rolldown, Node 24 LTS, pnpm 11, Tailwind 4 via @tailwindcss/vite, Bits UI 2, @lucide/svelte, TanStack Svelte Query 6, Vitest 4.1 + Testing Library Svelte, Cypress as browser authority. Current stable package lines verified for this slice are Svelte 5.56.10, SvelteKit 2.70.3, adapter-static 3.0.10, Vite 8.2.2, pnpm 11.25.0, svelte-check 4.7.6, Tailwind/@tailwindcss-vite 4.3.3, Bits UI 2.19.0, @lucide/svelte 1.37.0, @tanstack/svelte-query 6.1.48, @hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0, Testing Library Svelte 5.4.2. Stay on Vitest 4.1 (prefer current 4.1.x, not Vitest 5). Pin Hey API exactly because its own package guidance recommends exact pinning. Use TypeScript 6.0.2, not TypeScript 7. Do not use Bun, Yarn, Playwright, React, R3F or Babylon in apps/web. Scaffold apps/web as the target V3 app with its own package.json/packageManager pnpm@11.25.0, pnpm-lock.yaml, SvelteKit config, static SPA fallback, TypeScript config, Vite config, Tailwind CSS entry/theme tokens, accessible app shell, and basic route skeleton. The shell should visibly identify ED-Finder V3 and provide accessible navigation placeholders for the future product journey without pretending features are already ported. Establish TanStack Svelte Query at the app boundary. Add typed same-origin bootstrapping for GET /api/health and GET /api/auth/session; strongly prefer establishing the locked Hey API generated-client path now if it can be generated deterministically from the current FastAPI OpenAPI without making the normal web build depend on a live API. Do not create a large handwritten throwaway API layer. Preserve backend ownership of /api/*, exact /openapi.json and numeric /s/{id64}; Svelte owns all other application routes. Add component/unit coverage proving the shell renders, navigation is accessible and status states are handled. Add an apps/web Cypress config/spec that proves the built Svelte shell loads, representative Svelte routing works on direct navigation/refresh, and real same-origin health/session requests can be exercised against the disposable CI API. Update .github/workflows/ci.yml to add a Node-24/pnpm frozen-lock Svelte web job (install, svelte-check/typecheck, lint if configured, Vitest, build) while retaining the legacy React/Yarn job as reference coverage. Update .github/workflows/cypress-parity.yml so existing React Cypress parity remains intact AND a Svelte-foundation Cypress smoke runs against apps/web; fix the misleading Playwright job label only if safe in this same workflow, but do not remove historical Playwright suites/dependencies yet. Use the existing disposable backend/DB setup, never production. Add a focused repository contract test under tests/ that pins: apps/web is Svelte/SvelteKit/pnpm/Node24; frontend/ remains reference during migration; Cypress is browser authority; no Playwright/Babylon/React dependency enters apps/web; static output and backend route ownership are explicit. Update README/CLAUDE only as needed to identify apps/web as the new V3 implementation path while frontend/ remains reference. Keep Stage 27A boundaries unchanged. Validate at minimum: pnpm --dir apps/web install --frozen-lockfile (or equivalent from apps/web), svelte-check/typecheck, Vitest, build, the focused contract test, git diff --check, and any affected CI contract tests. If practical run the Svelte Cypress smoke locally against the disposable API; otherwise ensure the protected workflow is correctly wired. Inspect your final diff for scope creep. Commit all implementation changes to the target branch. In your final report include exact commit SHA, files changed, package versions, tests/results, any deliberate deferrals (especially Hey API generation if blocked by a concrete compatibility issue), and explicit confirmation that production, database state and Babylon runtime were untouched.
